comparison.why: YouTube publishes no benchmark for viewed-vs-swiped or retention; compare a Short with the channel's own Shorts once there are enough of them.

hook.fallbackSource: Vendor rules of thumb (70–90% viewed), no published method: low confidence, used only below minSample. https://www.creatorlanehq.com/blog/youtube-shorts-viewed-vs-swiped-away (2026-10-05)

retention.why: Above 100% means people rewatch; widely reported by creators, not confirmed by YouTube.

reach.why: Each Short is first shown to a small seed audience and spreads only on its response, so reach against the channel median says whether it left the seed.
reach.source: Todd Sherman (YouTube Shorts) on Creator Insider, reported by onlinemarketing.de 2026-08-31

format.why: No published decision rules exist; judging a format on 5–8 Shorts against the channel's own median avoids killing it on one unlucky post.
